original_value: AbstractMotivationTo characterize long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), both identifying and functionally annotating them are essential to be addressed. Moreover, a comprehensive construction for lncRNA annotation is desired to facilitate the research in the field.ResultsWe present LncADeep, a novel lncRNA identification and functional annotation tool. For lncRNA identification, LncADeep integrates intrinsic and homology features into a deep belief network and constructs models targeting both full- and partial-length transcripts. For functional annotation, LncADeep predicts a lncRNA’s interacting proteins based on deep neural networks, using both sequence and structure information. Furthermore, LncADeep integrates KEGG and Reactome pathway enrichment analysis and functional module detection with the predicted interacting proteins, and provides the enriched pathways and functional modules as functional annotations for lncRNAs. Test results show that LncADeep outperforms state-of-the-art tools, both for lncRNA identification and lncRNA–protein interaction prediction, and then presents a functional interpretation. We expect that LncADeep can contribute to identifying and annotating novel lncRNAs.Availability and implementationLncADeep is freely available for academic use at http://cqb.pku.edu.cn/ZhuLab/lncadeep/ and https://github.com/cyang235/LncADeep/.Supplementary informationSupplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

result.paraphrase: AbstractMotivationTo study long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), it is necessary to both identify them and annotate their functions. In addition, a complete lncRNA annotation framework is needed to support research in this area.ResultsWe introduce LncADeep, a new tool for lncRNA identification and functional annotation. For identification, LncADeep combines intrinsic and homology-based features in a deep belief network and builds models for both full-length and partial transcripts. For functional annotation, it uses deep neural networks with sequence and structure information to predict the proteins a lncRNA interacts with. It also incorporates KEGG and Reactome pathway enrichment analysis together with functional module detection for the predicted interacting proteins, using the enriched pathways and functional modules as lncRNA functional annotations. Benchmark results indicate that LncADeep surpasses current state-of-the-art tools in both lncRNA identification and lncRNA–protein interaction prediction, thereby providing functional interpretation. We anticipate that LncADeep will aid in identifying and annotating novel lncRNAs.Availability and implementationLncADeep is freely available for academic use at http://cqb.pku.edu.cn/ZhuLab/lncadeep/ and https://github.com/cyang235/LncADeep/.Supplementary informationSupplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.
